objectives.text: Amend the BSA compliance program requirements for supervised banks and rebrand them as anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) programs, aligned with concurrent FinCEN changes resulting from the AML Act of 2020.

citations.quote: The amended regulatory requirements, which will be referred to moving forward as anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) programs, align with changes that are being concurrently proposed by the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) as a result of the Anti-Money Laundering Act of 2020 (AML Act).

objectives.text: Incorporate a risk assessment process into AML/CFT program rules requiring consideration of national AML/CFT priorities published by FinCEN.

citations.quote: Incorporating a risk assessment process in AML/CFT program rules that would require, among other things, consideration of national AML/CFT priorities published by FinCEN.

objectives.text: Establish a standard for issuance of certain BSA-related enforcement and supervisory actions, including a consultation process with FinCEN.

citations.quote: Establishing a standard for the issuance of certain BSA-related enforcement and supervisory actions, including establishing a consultation process with FinCEN with respect to such actions.

obligations.action: establish and maintain a program that is reasonably designed to ensure compliance with the requirements of the BSA

citations.quote: The proposed rule continues to require banks to establish and maintain a program that is reasonably designed to ensure compliance with the requirements of the BSA, though with certain clarifications and changes.

obligations.action: prescribe regulations requiring banks to establish and maintain procedures reasonably designed to assure and monitor their compliance with the requirements of the BSA (independent mandate)

citations.quote: The agencies have an independent mandate to prescribe regulations requiring banks to establish and maintain procedures reasonably designed to assure and monitor their compliance with the requirements of the BSA.

obligations.actor: an agency intending to initiate an AML/CFT enforcement action or significant AML/CFT supervisory action
obligations.action: provide the director of FinCEN with an opportunity to review the action and consider any input offered by the director of FinCEN before initiating such an action
obligations.trigger: when one of the agencies intends to initiate an AML/CFT enforcement action or a significant AML/CFT supervisory action, as those terms are defined in the proposed regulation

citations.quote: Before initiating such an action, the agency would provide the director of FinCEN with an opportunity to review the action and would consider any input offered by the director of FinCEN.

obligations.action: satisfy customer due diligence (CDD) requirements incorporated into the program rules to reflect prior amendments to FinCEN's requirements

citations.quote: Including customer due diligence requirements to reflect prior amendments to FinCEN’s requirements.

the proposed rule explicitly incorporates customer due diligence (CDD) requirements that are currently set forth in FinCEN’s parallel regulations, harmonizing the requirements between the regulations.

citations.quote: FinCEN is amending its BSA compliance program rules to incorporate national AML/CFT priorities and other changes to the BSA pursuant to the AML Act.

notes: This item is a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (status: horizon / evidence role: supervisory_guidance); all obligations are prospective/proposed ('would', 'the proposed rule') rather than in force, and are extracted as written without harmonization. Obligations use conditional wording ('would require', 'would provide') reflecting proposal status; modality is mapped from underlying requiring language (require->must; contingent action before initiating an action->conditional). The text repeatedly notes definitions for 'AML/CFT enforcement action' and 'significant AML/CFT supervisory action' reside 'in the proposed regulation' not reproduced here, and the substantive prongs of the two-pronged 'established'/'maintained' framework are not given. Broker-dealers, MSBs, FINRA, and non-bank sectors are outside this OCC bulletin's coverage (banks only); those scope elements are not addressed by this source.
